result.title: C3: Rethinking Process Supervision via Confidence-Guided Credit Correction in Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Large language models are increasingly trained as multi-turn agents that interact with external tools. However, outcome-only reinforcement learning can produce a form of misguided reinforcement: even on successful trajectories, undesirable local behaviors may receive positive token-level advantages and be favored by the policy update. To address this issue, we propose Confidence-Guided Credit Correction (C$^3$), a plug-in method for local credit correction. C$^3$ identifies spans corresponding to undesirable behaviors and selectively corrects positive credit after advantage estimation, with the correction strength adaptively controlled by the behavior policy's confidence in the corresponding behavior, while leaving the task reward and original credit estimation unchanged. Across multiple multi-turn benchmarks, C$^3$ improves performance under both {critic-based and critic-free reinforcement learning methods}. Injecting the same behavioral signals as turn-level or outcome rewards does not consistently improve performance. Our results show that local credit correction provides an effective form of process supervision for outcome-driven RL.

AI.brief_summary: 针对多轮工具交互智能体中仅用结果奖励会误奖不良局部行为的问题，提出插件式方法 C3：定位对应不良行为的片段，并按行为策略对相应行为的置信度自适应修正优势估计中的正 credit，同时不改动任务奖励与原始 credit。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按片段做过程监督与 credit 修正」的思路，可能为 LVR 轨迹训练中的贡献分配、抑制无效推理片段提供可核查的方法线索；但论文面向纯文本多轮 RL，未涉及视觉状态或 latent 推理，迁移价值需进一步核查。
